tasks.title: Create SwiftPackageManagerKit Target and SPM Integration
tasks.description: Implement the SwiftPackageManagerKit library target for Swift Package Manager integration with models and execution layer
tasks.details:
Create SwiftPackageManagerKit target in Package.swift and implement core SPM integration:
1. Add new library target 'SwiftPackageManagerKit' with Foundation dependency
2. Implement SPMExecutor class using Process API to execute 'swift package dump-package' command
3. Create SPM JSON model classes (SPMPackageInfo, SPMProduct, SPMTarget, SPMDependency, SPMPlatform) matching the structure from swift package dump-package output
4. Implement SPMAnalyzer to parse JSON response using JSONDecoder with proper error handling
5. Add SPMValidator for validating package configurations
6. Create ProcessRunner utility for executing shell commands with timeout and proper error handling

Key implementation details:
- Use async/await for Process execution (available in Swift 5.5+)
- Model the JSON structure from 'swift package dump-package' output precisely
- Handle Process errors, timeouts, and non-zero exit codes
- Parse semantic version strings properly (e.g., "1.0.0"..<"2.0.0")
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for JSON parsing with fixture files containing sample dump-package outputs, integration tests for SPMExecutor with real swift package commands on test packages, validate error handling for malformed JSON and failed processes

subtasks.title: Add SwiftPackageManagerKit Target to Package.swift
subtasks.description: Configure the SwiftPackageManagerKit library target in Package.swift with required dependencies
subtasks.details: Edit Package.swift to add a new library target named 'SwiftPackageManagerKit' with Foundation as a dependency. Configure the target with proper source directory structure at Sources/SwiftPackageManagerKit/. Ensure the target is properly exposed as a library product for consumption by other targets in the package.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify Package.swift compiles successfully with swift package resolve, ensure target appears in swift package dump-package output

subtasks.title: Create SPM JSON Model Classes
subtasks.description: Implement Codable model classes matching the JSON structure from swift package dump-package output
subtasks.details: Create model classes in Sources/SwiftPackageManagerKit/Models/: SPMPackageInfo (root package structure with name, platforms, products, dependencies, targets), SPMProduct (type, name, targets array), SPMTarget (name, type, dependencies, path, sources, resources), SPMDependency (url/path, requirement with version ranges), SPMPlatform (platform name and version). All models must conform to Codable with proper CodingKeys for JSON mapping. Handle version requirement parsing for semantic version ranges like '1.0.0'..<'2.0.0'.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test each model with fixture JSON files containing real dump-package output, test encoding/decoding round trips, verify version range parsing

subtasks.title: Implement ProcessRunner Utility
subtasks.description: Create a reusable ProcessRunner class for executing shell commands with async/await support
subtasks.details: Implement ProcessRunner in Sources/SwiftPackageManagerKit/Utilities/ with async execute method that: creates and configures Process instances, sets up pipes for stdout/stderr capture, handles process termination with configurable timeout (default 30 seconds), returns ProcessResult struct containing exitCode, stdout, stderr strings, throws ProcessError for failures (timeout, non-zero exit, launch failure). Use Task for timeout handling and process cancellation support.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test with various shell commands (echo, ls, false), verify timeout handling with sleep command, test error cases and cancellation

subtasks.title: Implement SPMExecutor Class
subtasks.description: Create SPMExecutor to execute swift package commands and capture their output
subtasks.details: Implement SPMExecutor in Sources/SwiftPackageManagerKit/Execution/ with methods: dumpPackage(at packagePath: URL) async throws -> Data (executes 'swift package dump-package' and returns JSON data), resolvePackage(at packagePath: URL) async throws (executes 'swift package resolve'), buildPackage(at packagePath: URL) async throws (executes 'swift package build'). Use ProcessRunner for command execution, validate swift binary availability, handle working directory changes, provide detailed error messages for common failures.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test with real swift package commands on test fixtures, mock ProcessRunner for unit tests, verify error handling for invalid packages

subtasks.title: Implement SPMAnalyzer and SPMValidator
subtasks.description: Create analyzer for parsing SPM JSON and validator for package configuration validation
subtasks.details: Implement SPMAnalyzer in Sources/SwiftPackageManagerKit/Analysis/ with analyzePackage(data: Data) throws -> SPMPackageInfo method using JSONDecoder with proper error handling for malformed JSON. Create SPMValidator in Sources/SwiftPackageManagerKit/Validation/ with methods: validatePackageStructure(package: SPMPackageInfo) -> [ValidationIssue] (checks for missing products, orphaned targets, circular dependencies), validateVersionRequirements(dependencies: [SPMDependency]) -> [ValidationIssue] (validates semantic version ranges), validatePlatforms(platforms: [SPMPlatform]) -> [ValidationIssue] (ensures platform versions are valid).
subtasks.testStrategy: Test analyzer with various dump-package outputs including edge cases, test validator identifies common issues like circular dependencies and invalid versions

tasks.title: Implement Core PackageDSLManager SDK
tasks.description: Create the main PackageDSLManager class that serves as the primary SDK entry point for package manipulation
tasks.details:
Implement PackageDSLManager as the main SDK interface:
1. Create PackageDSLManager class with initialization for package URL
2. Implement createPackage(name:type:) method supporting library/executable/empty types
3. Add addTarget(name:type:dependencies:) for creating library/executable/test targets
4. Add addProduct(name:type:targets:) for creating library/executable products
5. Add addDependency methods supporting URL, path, and registry dependencies with version requirements
6. Implement removeTarget, removeProduct, removeDependency methods
7. Create internal SPMIntegrator wrapper to use SwiftPackageManagerKit
8. Add generatePackageSwift() method to create Package.swift from DSL
9. Implement validate() method comparing DSL against SPM metadata

Implementation approach:
- Store package configuration in memory as structured data
- Use builder pattern for fluent API design
- Integrate with existing PackageWriter for code generation
- Leverage SPMIntegrator for validation against actual SPM behavior
tasks.testStrategy: Test package creation with different types, verify CRUD operations for targets/products/dependencies maintain consistency, integration test generating Package.swift and validating with swift package dump-package, test error cases for invalid configurations

subtasks.title: Build product and dependency management

subtasks.details: Implement addProduct(name:type:targets:) using existing Product struct and ProductType enum. subtasks.title: Create removal and validation methods

tasks.title: Build Swift Settings Management System
tasks.description: Implement SwiftSettingsManager for managing Swift feature flags and unsafe compilation flags
tasks.details:
Create comprehensive Swift settings management:
1. Define SwiftFeature enum with all experimental features (StrictConcurrency, RegionBasedIsolation, etc.)
2. Define SwiftFeature enum with all upcoming features (GlobalConcurrency, InternalImportsByDefault, etc.)
3. Create UnsafeFlag enum covering compilation flags (O, Onone, WholeModuleOptimization), debug flags (G, ColorDiagnostics), emit flags (EmitModule, EmitIr), and warning flags
4. Implement parameterized flags (WarnLongFunctionBodies with milliseconds parameter)
5. Create SwiftSettingsManager class with methods to add/remove/list features and flags
6. Support target-specific and global Swift settings
7. Generate proper SwiftSettings DSL code using SwiftSyntaxBuilder

Current Swift 6.0 features to support:
- Experimental: StrictConcurrency can be both experimental and upcoming
- Handle .experimental() and .upcoming() modifiers properly
- Support parameterized unsafe flags with associated values
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test all flag combinations, verify generated DSL syntax is valid, test target-specific vs global settings precedence, validate parameterized flags with various values, integration test with actual Swift package compilation

subtasks.title: Define Swift Feature Enums
subtasks.description: Create SwiftFeature enum with experimental and upcoming feature cases
subtasks.details: Define comprehensive SwiftFeature enum in Sources/PackageDSLKit/SwiftFeature.swift with all experimental features (StrictConcurrency, RegionBasedIsolation, etc.) and upcoming features (GlobalConcurrency, InternalImportsByDefault, BareSlashRegexLiterals, ConciseMagicFile, ExistentialAny, ForwardTrailingClosures, ImplicitOpenExistentials, DisableOutwardActorInference). Implement proper case names, raw values, and methods to convert to SwiftSetting DSL calls like .enableExperimentalFeature() and .enableUpcomingFeature(). Include proper categorization between experimental and upcoming features.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test all feature cases can be converted to proper SwiftSetting syntax, verify experimental vs upcoming categorization is correct, test string representations match expected DSL output

subtasks.title: Create Unsafe Flags Enum System
subtasks.description: Implement UnsafeFlag enum covering all compilation, debug, emit, and warning flags
subtasks.details: Create UnsafeFlag enum in Sources/PackageDSLKit/UnsafeFlag.swift with compilation flags (O, Onone, WholeModuleOptimization), debug flags (G, ColorDiagnostics, DebugPrefixMap), emit flags (EmitModule, EmitIr, EmitAssembly), and warning flags (WarningsAsErrors, WarnLongFunctionBodies, WarnUnusedResult). Implement parameterized flags support with associated values (e.g., WarnLongFunctionBodies with milliseconds parameter). Create methods to generate proper .unsafeFlags() DSL calls with correct flag format (-O, -Onone, -whole-module-optimization, etc.).
subtasks.testStrategy: Test all flag types generate correct command-line arguments, verify parameterized flags handle values correctly, test conversion from camelCase to kebab-case flag format

subtasks.title: Build SwiftSettingsManager Class
subtasks.description: Implement core SwiftSettingsManager class for managing features and flags
subtasks.details: Create SwiftSettingsManager class in Sources/PackageDSLKit/SwiftSettingsManager.swift with properties to store active features and unsafe flags. Implement methods: addFeature(feature:target:), removeFeature(feature:target:), addUnsafeFlag(flag:target:), removeUnsafeFlag(flag:target:), listFeatures(target:), listUnsafeFlags(target:). Support both global and target-specific settings storage. Implement logic to handle precedence where target-specific settings override global ones. Create internal data structures to efficiently manage settings per target.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test adding/removing features and flags, verify target-specific vs global precedence, test listing methods return correct settings, validate duplicate prevention

subtasks.title: Implement SwiftSettings DSL Generation
subtasks.description: Create SwiftSyntaxBuilder integration for generating SwiftSettings DSL code
subtasks.details: Implement SwiftSettingsBuilder in Sources/PackageDSLKit/SwiftSettingsBuilder.swift using SwiftSyntaxBuilder to generate proper Package.swift SwiftSettings arrays. Create methods to convert SwiftSettingsManager state into SwiftSyntax nodes for .enableExperimentalFeature(), .enableUpcomingFeature(), and .unsafeFlags() calls. Handle proper formatting, indentation, and array syntax. Integrate with existing PackageWriter and ComponentBuildable protocols. Ensure generated code follows Swift Package Manager DSL conventions.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test generated DSL syntax compiles with swift package dump-package, verify all setting types generate valid syntax, test complex combinations of features and flags

subtasks.title: Integrate with PackageSpecifications
subtasks.description: Update PackageSpecifications and related types to support SwiftSettings
subtasks.details: Modify PackageSpecifications struct to properly handle swiftSettings array beyond just SwiftSettingRef references. Update PackageDirectoryConfiguration, Index, and PackageParser to parse and store SwiftSettings. Create proper TypeSource implementations for SwiftFeature and UnsafeFlag types. Update ComponentBuildable implementations for Target, TestTarget to include SwiftSettings in their build methods. Ensure SwiftSettings are properly serialized/deserialized in PackageFiles operations.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test full round-trip of parsing existing Package.swift with SwiftSettings, modifying settings, and regenerating valid Package.swift

tasks.title: Develop Platform Management System
tasks.description: Implement PlatformManager for year-based platform sets and individual platform specifications
tasks.details:
Build comprehensive platform support management:
1. Create PlatformSet enum with year-based mappings (2019-2024):
   - 2024: iOS 18+, macOS 15+, watchOS 11+, tvOS 18+, visionOS 2+
   - 2023: iOS 17+, macOS 14+, watchOS 10+, tvOS 17+, visionOS 1+
   - 2022: iOS 16+, macOS 13+, watchOS 9+, tvOS 16+
   - 2021: iOS 15+, macOS 12+, watchOS 8+, tvOS 15+
   - 2020: iOS 14+, macOS 11+, watchOS 7+, tvOS 14+
   - 2019: iOS 13+, macOS 10.15+, watchOS 6+, tvOS 13+
2. Implement PlatformManager class with set/remove/list operations
3. Support custom platform sets with include/exclude options
4. Add individual platform management (add/remove specific platforms)
5. Implement platform version validation
6. Generate SupportedPlatformSet and SupportedPlatform DSL code
7. Handle Linux and Windows platform specifications

Implementation details:
- Use existing SupportedPlatformSet type from codebase
- Map year to appropriate OS versions
- Support .when(platforms:) conditions for dependencies
tasks.testStrategy: Test all year-based platform sets generate correct versions, verify include/exclude filtering works correctly, test individual platform addition/removal, validate version string parsing and comparison, integration test with SPM validation

Each case should map to the appropriate platform versions as specified (e.g., 2024 -> iOS 18+, macOS 15+, etc.). Include helper methods to convert enum cases to Sets of SupportedPlatform instances. Implement CustomStringConvertible and CaseIterable for easy iteration and display.

subtasks.description: Connect both PlatformSetCommand and PlatformCommand to the existing SDK for reading and writing Package.swift files
subtasks.details: Use PackageParser to read current package configuration. Integrate with PackageWriter to persist platform changes. Update Package+Command.swift to register new commands in subcommands array. Ensure commands properly update PackageSpecifications with new platform configurations. Handle file I/O errors gracefully with appropriate error messages.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test full workflow from command to generated Package.swift, verify Package.swift syntax is valid after modifications, test error handling for missing or invalid Package.swift files

tasks.title: Create Package Validation and Generation Commands
tasks.description: Implement validate, generate, info, and doctor commands for package management
tasks.details:
Build package lifecycle and validation commands:
1. Implement ValidateCommand:
   - Execute 'swift package dump-package' via SPMIntegrator
   - Compare DSL structure with SPM metadata
   - Report mismatches, missing components, or inconsistencies
   - Return non-zero exit code on validation failure
2. Implement GenerateCommand:
   - Read PackageDSL from Package/ directory
   - Generate Package.swift using PackageWriter
   - Write to package root with proper swift-tools-version
   - Optionally run validation after generation
3. Implement InfoCommand:
   - Display package name, products, targets, dependencies
   - Show platform support and Swift settings
   - Format as readable summary or JSON output
4. Implement DoctorCommand:
   - Check for common issues (missing sources, circular dependencies)
   - Verify PackageDSL syntax is valid
   - Suggest fixes for common problems
   - Check swift-tools-version compatibility
tasks.testStrategy: Test validation catches DSL/SPM mismatches, verify generation creates valid Package.swift, test info command with various package configurations, verify doctor identifies common issues correctly

subtasks.title: Create ValidateCommand for Package Validation
subtasks.description: Implement the validate command that executes swift package dump-package and compares DSL with SPM metadata
subtasks.details: Create ValidateCommand.swift in Sources/package/Commands/ extending ParsableCommand. Implement validation logic that reads PackageDSL from Package/ directory using PackageParser, executes 'swift package dump-package' using Process API to get SPM metadata JSON, parses the JSON output into SPM model structures, compares DSL components with SPM data (products, targets, dependencies, platforms), reports any mismatches or inconsistencies to stdout with detailed error messages, and returns appropriate exit codes (0 for success, non-zero for validation failures). Include options for verbose output and JSON format reporting.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test with valid and invalid PackageDSL configurations, verify mismatch detection for missing targets, incorrect dependencies, and platform inconsistencies, test exit codes and error message formatting

subtasks.title: Implement GenerateCommand for Package.swift Generation
subtasks.description: Create command to generate Package.swift from PackageDSL files in Package/ directory
subtasks.details: Implement GenerateCommand.swift in Sources/package/Commands/ extending ParsableCommand. Parse PackageDSL from Package/ directory using PackageParser, use PackageWriter to generate Package.swift content with proper formatting, read swift-tools-version from .swift-version file or use default, write generated Package.swift to package root with appropriate header comment, add --validate flag to optionally run validation after generation using ValidateCommand logic, support --dry-run option to preview generated content without writing, handle file write errors gracefully with descriptive messages.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test generation with various PackageDSL configurations, verify generated Package.swift compiles with swift build, test dry-run mode outputs correct content without file writes, ensure validation flag works correctly

subtasks.title: Create InfoCommand for Package Information Display
subtasks.description: Implement info command to display package metadata in human-readable or JSON format
subtasks.details: Create InfoCommand.swift in Sources/package/Commands/ extending ParsableCommand. Execute 'swift package dump-package' to get current package metadata, parse JSON response into structured SPM models, display package information including name, platforms, products (with types and targets), targets (with dependencies and types), external dependencies (with version requirements), Swift language settings and flags. Support --format option for 'text' (default) or 'json' output, implement readable text formatting with proper indentation and sections, provide --verbose flag for additional details like target paths and resource specifications.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test with packages of varying complexity, verify JSON and text output formats are correct, test verbose mode shows additional details, ensure command handles missing Package.swift gracefully

subtasks.title: Implement DoctorCommand for Package Health Checks
subtasks.description: Create doctor command to diagnose common package issues and suggest fixes
subtasks.details: Implement DoctorCommand.swift in Sources/package/Commands/ extending ParsableCommand. Check for common issues: validate PackageDSL syntax by attempting to parse Package/ directory, verify Package.swift exists and is readable, check swift-tools-version compatibility with current Swift version, detect missing source files for declared targets, identify circular dependencies between targets, find orphaned targets not included in any product, validate dependency version requirements are satisfiable. Provide actionable fix suggestions for each issue found, support --fix flag for auto-fixing simple issues (like creating missing directories), output issues with severity levels (error, warning, info), return non-zero exit code if critical issues found.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test detection of various package issues like missing sources and circular dependencies, verify fix suggestions are accurate and actionable, test auto-fix functionality for simple issues, ensure proper exit codes based on issue severity

subtasks.title: Integrate Commands into Main CLI and Add Tests
subtasks.description: Wire up all validation commands to the main Package CLI and create comprehensive tests
subtasks.details: Update Package+Command.swift to register ValidateCommand, GenerateCommand, InfoCommand, and DoctorCommand as subcommands with proper help text and aliases. Create integration tests that validate a sample package with known issues, generate Package.swift and verify it matches expected output, run info command and parse its JSON output, execute doctor command and verify it identifies planted issues. Add unit tests for each command's option parsing and validation logic. Update command help documentation with usage examples and option descriptions. Ensure all commands follow consistent error handling and output formatting patterns.
subtasks.testStrategy: End-to-end testing of full command workflow from DSL to validation, test command composition (generate then validate), verify help text is comprehensive and accurate, test error handling across all commands

tasks.title: Implement Package Conversion from Traditional Package.swift
tasks.description: Create converter to transform traditional Package.swift files into PackageDSL format
tasks.details:
Build Package.swift to PackageDSL converter:
1. Implement ConvertCommand in CLI:
   - 'package convert <Package.swift>' or 'package convert' for current directory
   - Parse existing Package.swift using swift package dump-package
2. Create SPMToPackageDSL converter:
   - Map SPM JSON data to PackageDSL components
   - Convert products to Product structs
   - Convert targets to Target/TestTarget structs
   - Convert dependencies to Dependency structs
   - Map platforms to SupportedPlatformSet or individual platforms
   - Extract Swift settings and unsafe flags
3. Generate PackageDSL file structure:
   - Create Package/ directory with proper structure
   - Write component files using ComponentWriter
   - Generate index file with Package() definition
4. Implement RoundTripValidator:
   - Generate Package.swift from DSL
   - Compare with original using SPM dump
   - Report any data loss or differences
5. Handle edge cases:
   - Custom build settings
   - Complex dependency requirements
   - System libraries and binary targets
tasks.testStrategy: Test conversion with various Package.swift examples, verify round-trip conversion preserves all data, test edge cases like binary targets and system libraries, validate converted DSL generates identical Package.swift

subtasks.title: Create ConvertCommand CLI structure
subtasks.description: Implement the ConvertCommand class in the CLI with ArgumentParser integration for 'package convert' command
subtasks.details: Create ConvertCommand.swift in Sources/package/Commands/ following the pattern of existing commands (Initialize, Dump, Product). Implement ParsableCommand protocol with options for input Package.swift path (optional, defaults to current directory) and output directory. Add command to Package+Command.swift subcommands list. Include Settings option group for path configuration and FileManager access.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test command parsing with various argument combinations, verify default path handling when no arguments provided, test error cases for invalid paths

subtasks.title: Implement SPMPackageLoader for Package.swift parsing
subtasks.description: Create loader that executes 'swift package dump-package' and parses resulting JSON into structured data
subtasks.details: Create SPMPackageLoader.swift in Sources/PackageDSLKit/ that executes 'swift package dump-package' command using Process API, captures JSON output, and decodes it into Codable structs matching SPM's package description format. Define SPMPackage, SPMProduct, SPMTarget, SPMDependency structs matching the JSON schema. Handle process execution errors and JSON parsing failures gracefully.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test with sample Package.swift files of varying complexity, verify JSON parsing handles all SPM fields correctly, test error handling for malformed Package.swift files

subtasks.title: Build SPMToPackageDSL converter core
subtasks.description: Create converter that maps SPM package data structures to PackageDSL components
subtasks.details: Implement SPMToPackageDSLConverter.swift with methods to convert SPMPackage to PackageSpecifications. Map SPMProduct to Product with correct ProductType, SPMTarget to Target/TestTarget based on type, SPMDependency to Dependency handling URL/path/registry types with version requirements. Convert platforms array to SupportedPlatformSet or individual SupportedPlatform. Extract and map Swift language version, build settings, unsafe flags to appropriate DSL properties.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test each conversion method with various SPM configurations, verify all properties are mapped correctly, test edge cases like custom build settings and complex dependency requirements

subtasks.title: Generate PackageDSL file structure from converted data
subtasks.description: Use existing PackageWriter to create proper Package/ directory structure with component files
subtasks.details: Integrate SPMToPackageDSLConverter output with PackageWriter to generate file structure. Create Package/ directory at specified location, write component files (Products/, Dependencies/, Targets/, TestTargets/) using ComponentWriter, generate Index.swift with proper imports and Package() definition using PackageIndexWriter. Ensure proper file paths and directory creation using FileManager.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test file generation creates expected directory structure, verify generated files compile correctly, test that all components are properly written to their respective directories

subtasks.title: Implement RoundTripValidator for conversion verification
subtasks.description: Create validator that ensures converted PackageDSL generates equivalent Package.swift
subtasks.details: Create RoundTripValidator.swift that generates Package.swift from converted DSL using existing generation logic, executes 'swift package dump-package' on both original and generated Package.swift, compares the resulting JSON structures for equivalence. Report differences in products, targets, dependencies, platforms, or settings. Handle acceptable differences like ordering and whitespace. Provide detailed diff output for any data loss or transformation issues.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test round-trip validation with various Package.swift examples, verify validator detects data loss correctly, test that semantically equivalent but syntactically different Package.swift files pass validation

tasks.title: Add Advanced Error Handling and User Experience Enhancements
tasks.description: Implement comprehensive error handling, validation, and developer experience improvements
tasks.details:
Enhance error handling and developer experience:
1. Create custom error types with actionable messages:
   - PackageDSLError with specific cases for each failure type
   - SPMError for Swift Package Manager failures
   - ValidationError for configuration issues
2. Implement error recovery suggestions:
   - Suggest 'swift package resolve' for dependency issues
   - Provide fix commands for common problems
   - Show relevant documentation links
3. Add verbose and quiet modes:
   - '--verbose' flag showing detailed operations
   - '--quiet' flag suppressing non-error output
   - Progress indicators for long operations
4. Implement watch mode for development:
   - 'package watch' monitoring Package/ directory
   - Auto-regenerate Package.swift on changes
   - Run validation automatically
5. Add shell completions:
   - Generate completion scripts for bash/zsh/fish
   - Provide command and option suggestions
6. Create helpful diagnostics:
   - Color-coded output for errors/warnings/success
   - Diff view for validation mismatches
   - Dependency graph visualization

Use Swift 6.0 features:
- Structured concurrency for parallel operations
- AsyncSequence for watch mode
- Swift Testing framework for better test output
tasks.testStrategy: Test error messages are clear and actionable, verify watch mode detects file changes correctly, test shell completions work in different shells, validate verbose/quiet modes affect output appropriately, test error recovery suggestions are helpful

subtasks.title: Design Custom Error Type Hierarchy
subtasks.description: Create comprehensive error types with specific cases for different failure scenarios
subtasks.details: Extend the existing PackageDSLError enum with more specific error cases including SPMError for Swift Package Manager failures, ValidationError for configuration issues, FileSystemError for I/O operations, and DependencyError for dependency resolution issues. Each error case should include context information and suggested recovery actions. Define LocalizedError conformance with detailed error descriptions and recovery suggestions for each case.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test each error type with specific scenarios, verify error messages contain actionable information, test localized descriptions are clear and helpful

subtasks.title: Implement Verbose and Quiet Output Modes
subtasks.description: Add command-line flags to control output verbosity levels
subtasks.details: Modify Settings struct to add @Flag variables for --verbose and --quiet options. Create an OutputManager class that manages console output based on verbosity level. Implement methods for debug output (verbose only), regular output (default), error output (always shown), and quiet mode (errors only). Integrate with existing print statements in Initialize, Product, and Dump commands. Add progress indicators using Swift's AsyncStream for long-running operations like dependency resolution.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test that verbose flag shows detailed operations, verify quiet flag suppresses non-error output, ensure progress indicators appear for operations taking longer than 2 seconds

subtasks.title: Create Watch Mode for Development
subtasks.description: Implement file system monitoring to auto-regenerate Package.swift on changes
subtasks.details: Add a new Watch command to Package+Command that monitors the Package/ directory for changes. Implement using Darwin's FSEvents API or cross-platform file watching solution. Use AsyncSequence to handle file change events and debounce rapid changes. Auto-regenerate Package.swift when .swift files in Package/ directory change. Run validation automatically after regeneration and display results using the OutputManager. Support interruption with Ctrl+C gracefully.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test file change detection works reliably, verify debouncing prevents excessive regeneration, test graceful shutdown on interrupt signal, validate regenerated Package.swift matches expected output

subtasks.title: Add Shell Completion Support
subtasks.description: Generate and install completion scripts for bash, zsh, and fish shells
subtasks.details: Implement CompletionCommand using ArgumentParser's built-in completion generation capabilities. Add 'package completion' command that generates scripts for bash, zsh, and fish. Include installation instructions for each shell type. Enhance existing commands with completion annotations for better suggestions. Add custom completion logic for dynamic values like existing target names and dependency URLs. Create helper method to detect user's shell and provide tailored installation instructions.
subtasks.testStrategy: Generate completion scripts for each shell type and verify syntax, test completions work for all commands and options, verify dynamic completions suggest appropriate values

subtasks.title: Implement Diagnostic Output with Colors and Diffs
subtasks.description: Add color-coded output and diff visualization for better developer experience
subtasks.details: Create DiagnosticRenderer class that formats output with ANSI color codes when terminal supports it. Implement color schemes for errors (red), warnings (yellow), success (green), and info (blue). Add diff visualization for validation mismatches showing expected vs actual Package.swift content using a line-by-line diff algorithm. Create dependency graph visualization using ASCII art or simple tree structure. Integrate with OutputManager to respect verbose/quiet modes. Add --no-color flag to disable colors when needed.
